subject: tu:game/sys/sysservice
value: DATA GATE CLOSED for game/sys/sysservice (68.1% -> 100.0%). CAUSE: the TU's whole data gap was ONE section. Of 828 data bytes, extab(56)/extabindex(84)/.bss(344)/.sdata(24)/.sbss(56) were already 100%; .rodata (264 bytes) sat at 99.42857% and, because objdiff credits matched_data only for FULLY matched sections, contributed ZERO - the 264-byte section alone was the entire 264-byte gap. The .rodata bytes were BYTE-IDENTICAL between target and ours; the defect was that OUR object emitted 3 trailing zero bytes the target does not have, because the reconstructed `SysServiceStringPool` declared its last member `assertMessage[0x28]` (40) while the real object is 0x25 (37): 'Message: %s Press RESET to continue.' is 36 chars + NUL. Shrinking that one array to [0x25] made our section 261 bytes and closed the gap. GENERAL LESSON: a data section can be 100% byte-correct over its common prefix and still score under 100% purely on EXTENT, and datadiff.py will report it as `OK ... bytes compared` because datadiff compares our object against the DOL over the CLAIMED range and never sees that we emitted MORE than the object really contains. The instrument that shows it is an objdiff-cli one-shot diff of target-obj vs ours, reading section size on both sides. SECOND, UNRELATED DEFECT FOUND AND NOT FIXED (recorded as a live flip-blocker): sysservice.o carries THREE OWN-POOL UNDEFINED-SYMBOL GHOSTS. `powerpc-eabi-nm -u build/GUNE5D/src/game/sys/sysservice.o` lists lbl_80117708, lbl_80117770 and lbl_80117790 as UND, and all three addresses fall INSIDE sysservice's own .rodata splits range 0x801176B0..0x801177B8 - the exact pattern claim.law.symbolified-own-pool-literal-blocks-tu-flip.20260831.v1 defines as a TU-flip blocker. Origin: sysservice.c defines the whole 0x108 span as one `static const SysServiceStringPool lbl_801176B0` (line 95) while separately declaring lines 106-108 `extern const char lbl_80117708/lbl_80117770/lbl_80117790[]` and using them at lines 290/524/534, so the file both DEFINES and IMPORTS the same bytes; lbl_80117708 is literally the pool's `resetInvoked` member, which lines 199/244 reach as `lbl_801176B0.resetInvoked` - two spellings of one address in one TU, the duplicate-naming shape claim.reloc-symbol-sweep-image-census.20260831.v1 found in attract.c. THIS DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS that census's summary sentence 'IMAGE-WIDE RESULT OF THAT SCREEN: ZERO of the 59 NonMatching TUs carry an own-pool UND ghost ... mb_tree was the only instance and it is fixed' (repeated in claim.flip-ranking-table-and-corrected-own-pool-screen.20260831.v1). The screen's DISCRIMINANT is sound and was re-run here unchanged; only its 'zero remaining' RESULT is refuted, so the image-wide sweep should be re-run before any flip-readiness conclusion rests on it. SUGGESTED FIX, not attempted this run because it restructures a TU with 16 already-matched functions: split the one struct into four objects on the target's own boundaries (0x58 / 0x68 / 0x20 / 0x25) named lbl_801176B0, lbl_80117708, lbl_80117770, lbl_80117790 so the TU DEFINES all four and imports none; the byte accounting 88+104+32+37 = 261 already checks out, and the member references at lines 199/244/290 would move onto the second struct.
